detailed_analysis: The spectrum is dominated by an intense band at 142.18 +/- 0.01 cm-1 (FWHM 8.1 cm-1, mixed eta~0.50) with a genuine asymmetric low-frequency shoulder near 135 cm-1. This is the anatase TiO2 Eg mode (~144 cm-1), by far the most intense Raman feature of anatase. The remaining strong, well-constrained bands fall at 395.3 (Eg/B1g region ~399), 514.4 (overlapping A1g+B1g ~516), and 636.4 cm-1 (Eg ~639). The weak feature at ~199 cm-1 corresponds to the weak anatase Eg mode near 197 cm-1 (often near detection limit). This full five-band set, in the correct intensity ordering (142 >> 395 > 515 > 637 >> 197), constitutes a definitive anatase fingerprint per the TiO2 diagnostic bands (anatase 144 very strong + 399/516/639 + weak 197); crucially there is NO band at 447/612 (rutile) and no 235/612 rutile signature, so the polymorph is anatase, not rutile. The 300/310 doublet, 375 shoulder, and 790 band are weak, poorly constrained (large fractional errors, parameters pinned at bounds/caps) and are best regarded as fitting artifacts, minor disorder features, or possible second-order/combination scattering rather than diagnostic modes; they should not be over-interpreted. The near-zero linear baseline and low baseline area fraction (0.206) confirm minimal fluorescence, consistent with a well-crystallized oxide. Residual excursions in the inter-peak valleys arise from linear-baseline + pseudo-Voigt wing behavior and residual asymmetry on the strongest peak; they are small in absolute terms (zoom fits look excellent) and do not alter the identification. Machine-readable band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): 142.2 (1.00), 395.3 (0.70), 514.4 (0.57), 636.4 (0.093), 199.1 (0.014), 794.5 (0.021), 383 (0.15, ill-constrained shoulder), 292/312 (~0.01, ill-constrained).

scientific_claims.claim: The unknown compound is anatase-phase TiO2, identified by its diagnostic Raman band set at 142.18 +/- 0.01, 199.1 +/- 1.0, 395.3 +/- 0.2, 514.4 +/- 0.03, and 636.4 +/- 0.15 cm-1 (Eg/B1g/A1g modes), with the dominant Eg mode at 142.18 +/- 0.01 cm-1 (FWHM 8.1 +/- 0.1 cm-1).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Definitive, non-destructive phase identification distinguishing anatase from rutile/brookite is critical for photocatalysis, pigments, and battery/sensor materials where polymorph controls function; the sharp low-FWHM Eg mode also indicates good crystallinity and small strain.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone identified anatase TiO2 by its characteristic Raman Eg mode near 142 cm-1 together with the 197/399/516/639 cm-1 band set, and used the main-band position/width to assess crystallinity and phase purity?

model_type: Sum of 10 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a linear (near-zero) baseline, fit over the full range with Levenberg-Marquardt (least_squares TRF). Inventory: shoulder_128 + peak_141 (asymmetric main band), sharp peak_194, resolved 300/310 doublet, shoulder_375 + peak_395, peak_515, peak_637, peak_790. Centers bounded +/-8-10 cm-1; per-band FWHM caps (doublet <=25 cm-1); not fluorescence-dominated (rolling-min baseline area fraction = 0.206).

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 8 pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear (near-zero, low-slope) baseline. Components at approximately 145, 195, 300, 310, 395, 515, 637, and 790 cm-1 — the single ~305 band is replaced by a resolved doublet at ~300 and ~310 to capture the flat-topped structure. Remaining bands each modeled as a single symmetric pseudo-Voigt (395 and 637 confirmed clean/symmetric in their zoom windows).

issues.problem: The dominant peak is under-resolved: a single pseudo-Voigt (peak_1, eta=1, pure Lorentzian, FWHM=11.4) cannot reproduce the asymmetric peak shape with its broad shoulder near ~125-130 cm-1.
The 394 cm-1 peak's rising edge and apex are systematically misfit; the model lacks a component to describe the shoulder on the low-x rising flank near ~370-380.
Systematic curvature residual around the 514 band.
peak_3 sits at its center bound (290) with center_err=28 and FWHM pinned at the 50 cap; peak_4 has amplitude_err > amplitude and eta≈0 — these components are poorly determined.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Re-seed/adjust components to capture the low-x shoulder of the 141 cm-1 peak (~127-130) and the rising shoulder of the 394 peak (~375), and re-seed the 300/310 doublet within bounds; also allow the main peak's shape (eta/FWHM) to better track its asymmetry.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear (near-zero, low-slope) baseline. Core band centers remain at approximately 145, 195, 300, 310, 395, 515, 637, and 790 cm-1 as locked by the plan. Within this locked model, the profile inventory is refined to better resolve documented sub-structure: (1) the strong 141/145 cm-1 band is described with the existing pseudo-Voigt plus a re-purposed component seeded on its low-x shoulder near ~127-130 cm-1 to capture the observed asymmetric tail; (2) the 395 cm-1 band is accompanied by a component on its rising low-x flank near ~375 cm-1 to describe the shoulder on the rising edge; (3) the flat-topped ~305 feature remains a resolved doublet at ~300 and ~310 cm-1, but with re-seeded centers pulled inside their bounds and physically reasonable, non-pinned widths; (4) the 515 cm-1 band retains its single pseudo-Voigt with refined width/shape (eta/FWHM) to eliminate curvature residual; (5) the ~194 cm-1 sharp feature and the weak ~700/637 region are given improved initial guesses so their components are well-determined rather than parked on noise. All components remain pseudo-Voigt on a linear baseline — no new band-type or model class is introduced beyond re-seeding and shape adjustment within the existing profile set.

issues.problem: Symmetric pseudo-Voigt slightly under-fits the wings/tail asymmetry of the 515 band
Minor systematic oscillation on the flanks of the dominant peak
